newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ex-soccer star Pele named as U.N. leprosy envoy.
newsitem.headline: Ex-soccer star Pele named as U.N. leprosy envoy.

text.p: Former Brazilian soccer star Pele was named by the World Health Organisation on Friday as a "goodwill ambassador" for eliminating leprosy around the world.
The 57-year-old Pele, whose real name is Edson Arantes do Nascimento, was widely regarded as the greatest footballer in the world in the 1960s and is currently Brazil's Minister of Sport.

He is already actively involved in the fight against leprosy in Brazil -- which with a total of 106,000 registered cases of the wasting disease is the second worst leprosy-hit country in the world after India, which has 500,000.
WHO officials say the global total of known cases is 1.15 million.
Many African, Asian and Latin American countries where leprosy is endemic have launched campaigns to eliminate it by the year 2000 with assistance from the WHO.

Officials at the U.N. agency said Pele would be lending his globally-known name and high profile to promote these campaigns and encourage sufferers -- who are often hidden by their communities -- to come forward for treatment.
